account:
Today has been mostly routine, with persistent but unverified talk of a bridge or port change. Several townsfolk repeated vague reports pointing to the bakery and the inn, but nobody has supplied concrete details or firsthand evidence to me. The neighbour told me she checked with the baker, who knew of no confirmed changes; the secretary likewise regards the talk as unsubstantiated. I do not know whether there is an actual proposal behind it, or what purpose it would serve, so I should not treat the repetition as confirmation.

I attended the ten o'clock mill inspection, but could not locate the miller or obtain grain figures. The inspection remains incomplete, and I asked the secretary to request another appointment. No council letters had arrived when I returned for the one o'clock correspondence appointment. The secretary has been keeping the appointment book and receiving correspondence.

I kept my three o'clock tea appointment at the neighbour's dockside cottage. She said the baker had stocked his stall and reported plenty of bread. She had personally seen nothing unusual along the docks, though she had been home since late morning and could not account for everything outside. There is no verified connection between the bread supply and the bridge or port gossip. I have now returned to town hall at about four thirty for my office appointment; the secretary is nearby. My next scheduled destination is home at seven.
